mainTopic: Who acquires a dead גר's rights and property (miscarriage payments, documents, collateral), and the start of the laws of a pit that crosses domains
overview: The גמרא finishes fixing a ברייתא to read 'זכתה' (she acquires). It then asks whether two ברייתות, one saying חייב and one saying פטור, match the argument between רבה and רב חסדא. The case is someone who injures the pregnant wife of a גר after the גר has died. רב חסדא can explain both ברייתות in his favor, in two different ways. The second way separates שבח ולדות, which the woman gets because she already had a share, from דמי ולדות, which she never shared and so does not get. Next, רב ייבא סבא and רב נחמן discuss whether someone who grabs a dead גר's loan documents acquires the paper itself. רבה then rules on collateral held when a גר dies, and the גמרא limits קנין חצר to an owner who is nearby. A new משנה follows about a pit dug in one domain and opened into another. רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא disagree about which case is the Torah's בור, and רבה begins explaining exactly where they disagree, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: read it as 'she acquires'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes a word in the ברייתא it was discussing, from 'זכה' (he acquires) to 'זכתה' (she acquires).
steps.simpleTranslation: And change the wording of the ברייתא to read: 'She acquires.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its previous discussion by correcting one word in a ברייתא. Instead of saying the damager 'acquires' (keeps the money), read it as saying the woman 'acquires' it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא as worded said 'זכה', meaning the damager keeps the payment because there is no one to collect it. Changing it to 'זכתה' means the woman herself collects. This one-letter change turns the damager from פטור into someone who must pay her.

keyTerms.meaning: She acquires (she is entitled to the money)
He acquires (here, the damager keeps the money)

phrases.english: And teach it as: 'She acquires.'
phrases.notes: The ברייתא was saying 'he acquires,' meaning the damager. The גמרא says to read it as 'she acquires,' meaning the woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנִי: ״זָכְתָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion from before this section by correcting the wording of a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should read 'זכתה': the woman, not the damager, gets the payment.

steps.title: Is this an old argument between two ברייתות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument between רבה and רב חסדא is the same as an argument between two ברייתות about hurting a pregnant woman after her husband, a גר, has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like an argument between תנאים. A Jewish woman married a גר, became pregnant from him, and someone injured her. If it happened while the גר was alive, the damager pays the miscarriage money to the גר. If it happened after the גר died, one ברייתא says the damager is חייב and another says he is פטור. Isn't this an argument between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that disagree about whether the damager must pay after the גר has died. It suggests that our two אמוראים are simply repeating this older argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the גר is alive, everyone agrees he collects the miscarriage money. After he dies, the ברייתות split between חייב and פטור. The גמרא wants to line up רבה and רב חסדא with these two sides, which would show their argument is really between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it matches an argument between תנאים
A convert to Judaism
Payment for the unborn babies lost in a miscarriage
One ברייתא teaches
Injured

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות agree that while the גר is alive, he collects the money. The only disagreement is about what happens after his death.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים:
phrases.notes: He means the argument between רבה and רב חסדא from earlier.

phrases.english: A Jewish woman who was married to a convert
and she became pregnant from him, and someone injured her,
during the lifetime of the convert,
he gives the payment for the miscarried babies to the convert.
After the death of the convert,
one ברייתא teaches: he is liable,
and one ברייתא teaches: he is exempt.
What, is it not a dispute between תנאים?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the wording, the גמרא steps back and asks whether the whole argument already existed among תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the argument between רבה and רב חסדא simply match the two ברייתות that say חייב and פטור?

steps.title: For רבה it is an argument, but must it be one for רב חסדא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that for רבה this is clearly an argument between תנאים, and asks whether רב חסדא is also forced to say so.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבה, it is certainly an argument between תנאים. But according to רב חסדא, must we say it is an argument between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question. רבה clearly agrees with one ברייתא and disagrees with the other. The real question is whether רב חסדא must also pick a side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, the two ברייתות cannot both fit his view, so one ברייתא is against him and he follows the other. The גמרא now checks whether רב חסדא can avoid this by explaining both ברייתות in a way that fits him. This sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly
Must we say? (is it really so?)

phrases.english: According to Rabba, it is certainly a dispute between תנאים.
But according to Rav Ḥisda,
shall we say that it is a dispute between תנאים?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּה וַדַּאי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא אֶלָּא לְרַב חִסְדָּא מִי לֵימָא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 2: it is clear for רבה, but open for רב חסדא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can רב חסדא explain both ברייתות so that they fit his view?

steps.title: Both ברייתות fit רב חסדא: one follows the רבנן, one follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא can say the ברייתות are about the woman's increased value from pregnancy. The one that says פטור follows the רבנן, and the one that says חייב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows the רבנן, and that ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא does not have to take sides. The two ברייתות are arguing about a different topic, the same one the רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ברייתות are read as talking about the extra value a pregnancy adds to the woman, not the payment for the lost babies. The רבנן give that extra value to the husband, so once he dies the damager is פטור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives the woman a share, so the damager is חייב to pay her.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (here comes an answer)
This one ... that one
The Sages (the majority view in the משנה)

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this one follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says פטור. The רבנן of our משנה give the pregnancy's added value to the husband.

phrases.english: that one follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא רַבָּנַן הָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by showing that רב חסדא can fit both ברייתות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ברייתא to a different side of the argument in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to argue about the same thing as רבה and רב חסדא, so רב חסדא would have to reject one of them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות argue about the pregnancy's added value, following the רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so רב חסדא needs to reject neither.

steps.title: Why mention 'after death' if she already gets half while he is alive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the woman gets a share even while her husband is alive, so why does the ברייתא speak only about after his death?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, why speak specifically about after death? Even while he is alive, she also has half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the answer it just gave. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives the woman a share anyway, then saying 'after the גר's death' seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was explained as giving the woman half of the pregnancy's value even during the husband's life. If so, the ברייתא that says חייב should not need the case of the husband's death to make her get paid. The challenge is that the detail 'after death' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case?
During his lifetime
Half

phrases.english: If it follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
why speak specifically about after death?

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ מֵחַיִּים נָמֵי אִית לַהּ פַּלְגָא!
phrases.english: Even during his lifetime she also has half!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַאי אִרְיָא לְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4 by asking about the detail 'after death'.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the ברייתא that says חייב 'after the death of the גר' to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives the woman a share even during the husband's life, so limiting the ruling to after his death seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Half while he is alive, all of it after his death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that during the husband's life the woman gets half, but after his death she gets all of it. That difference is why the ברייתא mentions after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: During his lifetime she has half. After his death, she has all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why 'after death' matters. The detail changes how much she gets, from half to the whole amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the husband and wife share the pregnancy's value while he is alive. Once the גר dies, there is no husband or heir to take his half, so the whole amount goes to her. The ברייתא mentions the case after death to teach that she gets the full payment.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it
After death

steps.whatToRemember: רבה must say the two ברייתות are an argument between תנאים. רב חסדא can explain both as being about the pregnancy's added value: פטור follows the רבנן, and חייב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, she gets half while her husband lives and all of it after he dies.

phrases.english: During his lifetime she has half,
after his death, all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵחַיִּים אִית לַהּ פַּלְגָא לְאַחַר מִיתָה כּוּלֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by showing that 'after death' changes her share from half to all.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the detail matters because the amount is different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning 'after death' seemed pointless, because she gets a share in any case.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the husband's death she gets the full amount, not just half, so the detail is needed.

steps.title: Second answer: both ברייתות follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to explain the two ברייתות. Both follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but one is about the increase in the woman's value (שבח ולדות) and the other is about payment for the lost babies (דמי ולדות).
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say both ברייתות follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The one that says חייב is about the extra value the pregnancy added to the woman. The one that says פטור is about the payment for the babies themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer for רב חסדא. The two ברייתות do not argue, because they are talking about two different payments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the two ברייתות were split between the רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Now both are placed under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. שבח ולדות partly belongs to the woman, so after the husband dies she gets all of it. דמי ולדות belongs only to the husband, so once the גר husband dies, nobody can collect it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
This one and that one, meaning both sources
The extra value the pregnancy adds to the woman
The payment for the babies that were lost

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two payments. שבח ולדות is the extra value of the pregnant woman herself. דמי ולדות is payment for the babies that were lost.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא וְהָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל;
phrases.english: this one and that one both follow Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel;
here, it is about the increase in value from the offspring,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says חייב, because the woman herself collects this money.

phrases.english: there, it is about the payment for the offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer instead of the one in steps 4 through 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: both ברייתות follow one תנא, but each speaks about a different payment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to argue, as if they followed two different opinions
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The woman collects שבח ולדות, and nobody collects דמי ולדות

steps.title: Challenge: the two payments should follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two payments should be different. If the woman gets שבח ולדות after her husband dies, she should also get דמי ולדות. And then the רבנן should agree too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Let us learn the rule for the payment for the babies from the rule for the increase in value. And let us learn what the רבנן hold from what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second answer. It argues that the two payments should not be treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the woman takes over the husband's share of שבח ולדות after he dies, then she should also take over דמי ולדות. And since the רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל do not argue about דמי ולדות, the רבנן should hold the same way. Then the split between the ברייתות falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be learned (from another case)
The Sages who argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

phrases.english: They said:
from the increase in value from the offspring, let us learn the payment for the offspring,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לִישְׁמַע לְרַבָּנַן!
phrases.english: and from Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel let us learn the opinion of the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מִשְּׁבַח וְלָדוֹת לִישְׁמַע דְּמֵי וְלָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference step 7 made between שבח ולדות and דמי ולדות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both payments come from the same pregnancy. So if the woman takes over one after her husband dies, she should take over the other too, and the רבנן should agree.

steps.title: Answer: she gets only what she already had a share in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is a real difference. She already had a share in שבח ולדות, so she gets all of it after her husband dies. She never had a share in דמי ולדות, so she gets none of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: No. The increase in value is something she already has a hand in, so she gets all of it. The payment for the babies is something she has no hand in, so she gets none of it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the second answer. It explains why the two payments really are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that she can take over the husband's part only where she already had a part of her own. With שבח ולדות she had half even while he was alive, so after his death it all goes to her. With דמי ולדות she never had any part, so she has no more claim than anyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: She has a hand in them, meaning she already owns a share
She acquires
At all

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, after the גר husband dies the woman gets all of שבח ולדות, because she already owned part of it. She gets none of דמי ולדות, because she never owned any of it.

phrases.english: They said: No;
the increase in value from the offspring, in which she has a share,
she acquires all of it;

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵי וְלָדוֹת, לָא שָׁיְיכָא יְדַהּ בְּגַוַּיְיהוּ –
phrases.english: the payment for the offspring, in which she has no share,
she does not acquire it at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא; שְׁבַח וְלָדוֹת, דְּשָׁיְיכָא יְדַהּ בְּגַוַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a real difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both payments come from the pregnancy, so they should follow the same rule
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman takes over only what she already partly owned. So she gets all of שבח ולדות and none of דמי ולדות

steps.title: New question: grabbing the loan documents of a dead גר
steps.stepSummary: רב ייבא סבא asks רב נחמן about someone who grabs the loan documents of a גר who died with no heirs. Does that person acquire them? He may have wanted only the land the document stands for and not the paper itself. Or he may also have meant to acquire the paper.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rav Yeiva the Elder asked Rav Naḥman: Someone takes hold of a convert's documents. What is the law? Maybe a person who grabs a document really wants the land. He did not grab the land, and he does not get the paper either, because he was not thinking about the paper. Or maybe he did also mean to get the paper?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins here. רב ייבא סבא asks רב נחמן a question about a dead גר's loan documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a גר dies with no heirs, his property is ownerless, and whoever grabs it first owns it. The question is about his loan documents. If the person who grabs them only wanted the land behind the document, he gets nothing, not the land and not the paper. If he also wanted the paper, he at least owns the paper.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (raised a question to him)
One who takes possession
A written document, here a loan document
His intention, what he had in mind
Or perhaps: introduces the other side of a question

steps.whyThisMatters: This question depends on what the person was thinking when he took the item. His intention decides what he actually acquires.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב יֵיבָא סָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yeiva the Elder asked Rav Naḥman:
one who takes possession of the documents of a convert, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The convert has died with no heirs, so his things belong to nobody and anyone can take them.

phrases.english: one who takes possession of a document
takes possession with the land in mind,
phrases.notes: He means the land that is pledged to pay back the loan written in the document.

phrases.english: and he did not take possession of the land;
and he also did not acquire the document,
because his intention was not on the document;
or perhaps his intention was also on the document?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב יֵיבָא סָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the property of a dead גר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a person who grabs a dead גר's loan documents acquire them? This depends on whether he meant to acquire only the land or also the paper.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Who wants the paper itself?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רב ייבא סבא with a rhetorical question. Does the person need the document just to cover the opening of his jar?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Answer this, my master: does he need the document to cover the opening of his flask?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן responds to the question from Step 10. He suggests that nobody grabs a document because he wants the paper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 asked whether the grabber also meant to acquire the paper itself. רב נחמן says the paper alone is almost worthless; at most it could plug a jar. So he assumes the grabber only wanted what the document stands for, and he did not mean to acquire the paper.

keyTerms.meaning: Answer, my master (a respectful way of opening a reply)
To tie up, to cover or seal
The opening of a small jar or flask

phrases.english: He said to him: Answer, my master,
is it to cover the opening of his flask
that he needs it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָצוֹר עַל פִּי צְלוֹחִיתוֹ הוּא צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ייבא סבא's question by rejecting the second option: that the grabber wanted the paper.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the grabber also intend to acquire the paper of the document?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Unlikely. The paper by itself is only good for covering a jar, so he must have wanted only what the document stands for.

steps.title: רב ייבא סבא: Yes, even to cover a jar
steps.stepSummary: רב ייבא סבא pushes back. A person does want the paper, even for a small use like covering a jar.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, to cover, and to cover.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ייבא סבא rejects רב נחמן's reasoning. He says the grabber may indeed want the paper for such a simple use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן assumed that a small, everyday use is not worth acquiring. רב ייבא סבא answers that even a small use like that is real, so the grabber does mean to acquire the paper too. With that, the exchange ends, and the גמרא moves on to רבה's teaching about collateral.

keyTerms.meaning: To cover, and indeed to cover: a doubled word stressing 'yes, even for that'

phrases.english: He said to him: to cover, and to cover.
phrases.notes: Repeating the word means: yes, even for something as small as plugging a jar, he wants it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָצוֹר וְלָצוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's assumption in Step 11 that nobody wants the bare paper.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב נחמן's reasoning that the paper has no value worth acquiring.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even a small, everyday use like covering a jar is a real reason to want the paper.

steps.title: A Jew's collateral held by a גֵּר who died
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules on a case where a גֵּר lent money to a Jew and held his collateral, and then the גֵּר died. If someone else grabs the collateral, it is taken from him, because the גֵּר's lien ended when he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: If a Jew's collateral was in the hands of a גֵּר, and the גֵּר died, and another Jew came and took hold of it, we take it away from him. Why? Once the גֵּר died, his lien on it ended.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins a new teaching about collateral. In this first case, the collateral belongs to a Jew and is held by the גֵּר who lent him money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גֵּר never owned the collateral; he only had a lien (שִׁעְבּוּד) on it to secure his loan. When he died without heirs, that lien simply disappeared. The item goes back to its real owner, the borrower, so it was never ownerless, and the grabber has no claim to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Collateral: an item a borrower gives the lender as security
A convert. One who dies without children born after his conversion has no heirs.
Took hold of it, took possession of it
We take it out of his hands
A lien: the lender's legal claim on the item for his loan
Ended, was cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the collateral belonged to the גֵּר. He only held it as security. Once his claim ends, it belongs fully to the Jew who gave it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַשְׁכּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיַד גֵּר,
phrases.english: Rabba said: The collateral of a Jew in the hand of a convert,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵת הַגֵּר, וּבָא יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֵר וְהֶחְזִיק בּוֹ –
phrases.english: and the convert died, and another Jew came and took hold of it –
we take it out of his hand.
What is the reason?
Since the convert died –
his lien is cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַשְׁכּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיַד גֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about a dead גֵּר's property, this time collateral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew's collateral held by a גֵּר who died goes back to the Jew, because the גֵּר's lien ended. A grabber must return it.

steps.title: A גֵּר's collateral held by a Jew
steps.stepSummary: In the reverse case, a Jew lent money to a גֵּר and holds his collateral, and then the גֵּר died. If someone else grabs it, the lender keeps the value of his loan and the grabber takes the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a גֵּר's collateral was in the hands of a Jew, and the גֵּר died, and another Jew came and took hold of it, this one (the lender) acquires the amount of his money, and that one (the grabber) acquires the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the opposite case. Now the collateral belongs to the גֵּר and is held by the Jewish lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the item really belonged to the גֵּר, so when he died with no heirs it became ownerless. The lender's lien still protects the amount he lent. Anything worth more than the loan is ownerless, and the grabber takes it.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount equal to his money (the loan)
The rest, the extra value beyond the loan
Acquired

phrases.english: The collateral of a convert in the hand of a Jew,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵת הַגֵּר, וּבָא יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֵר וְהֶחֱזִיק בּוֹ –
phrases.english: and the convert died, and another Jew came and took hold of it –
this one acquires as much as his money,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the lender who was holding the item.

phrases.english: and that one acquires the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁכּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל גֵּר בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's teaching with the reverse case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a גֵּר's collateral is held by a Jewish lender and the גֵּר dies, the lender keeps the value of his loan, and whoever grabs it takes the extra.

steps.title: Why doesn't the lender's courtyard acquire everything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה. The collateral sits in the lender's possession, so his חָצֵר should acquire the whole thing for him, since רבי יוסי בר חנינא says a person's חָצֵר acquires for him even without his knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let his courtyard acquire it for him! After all, רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: A person's courtyard acquires for him even without his knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second case in Step 14. It asks why the lender doesn't get the extra value too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra value became ownerless while it was sitting in the lender's domain. By the rule of קִנְיַן חָצֵר, his property should acquire ownerless things for him automatically, even if he does not know about it. If so, the grabber should get nothing, which contradicts רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: But why? (opens a challenge)
A courtyard, or any property a person owns
Acquiring an item because it is inside one's property
Without his knowledge

phrases.english: But why? Let his courtyard acquire it for him –
for didn't Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina say:
A person's courtyard acquires for him
without his knowledge!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? תִּקְנֵי לֵיהּ חֲצֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's ruling in Step 14 that the grabber gets the extra value.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the grabber acquires the value beyond the loan.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The collateral is in the lender's domain. Under רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule, his חָצֵר should acquire the ownerless extra for him automatically, leaving nothing for the grabber.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step, where the גמרא must explain why קִנְיַן חָצֵר does not work for the lender here.

steps.title: A courtyard acquires only when its owner is nearby
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבה is talking about a case where the lender is not there. A חָצֵר only acquires for its owner when he himself could have acquired the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: we are talking about a case where the lender is not there. Whenever he is there, so that he could take the item himself, his courtyard also acquires it for him. Whenever he is not there, so that he could not take it himself, his courtyard does not acquire it either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. רבה's case is one where the lender is not standing near his courtyard, so his חָצֵר does not acquire the rest of the collateral for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that a חָצֵר always acquires, following רבי יוסי בר חנינא. The answer limits that rule: the חָצֵר works like the owner's hand. It acquires only when the owner himself, standing there, could have picked the item up and acquired it. If he is away, the courtyard does nothing, so the grabber may take whatever is beyond the loan.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a ruling to a specific case)
Where he is not there
Where he is there
His courtyard acquires for him
He is able to acquire

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule that a חָצֵר acquires without the owner knowing. He may not know the item is there, but he has to be close enough that he could have taken it.

phrases.english: They say: With what are we dealing here?
Where he is not there.
phrases.notes: "He" is the lender who holds the collateral in his courtyard.

phrases.english: Anywhere that he himself is there,
so that if he wants to acquire, he is able to acquire,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; they belong to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: his courtyard also acquires for him;
anywhere that he himself is not there,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי בָּעֵי הוּא לְמִיקְנֵי לָא מָצֵי קָנֵי –
phrases.english: so that if he wanted to acquire, he could not acquire,
his courtyard also does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 15 against רבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): רבה's ruling is about a lender who is not present.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חָצֵר always acquires for its owner, so the lender should get the whole collateral.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חָצֵר acquires only when the owner is close enough to acquire the item himself. Here he is away, so it does not.

steps.title: The ruling: if he is not there, his courtyard does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that when the lender is not present at his courtyard, he does not acquire the rest of the collateral.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: when he is not in his courtyard, he does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. If the owner is not in or near his courtyard, the courtyard does not acquire for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the answer of step 16 the practical הלכה. So in רבה's case the lender keeps only the amount of his loan, and the grabber keeps the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical law is
In his courtyard
He did not acquire

steps.whatToRemember: A חָצֵר works for its owner only when he is nearby and could have acquired the item himself. When he is away, it does not acquire for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical limit on קנין חצר, acquiring through one's property, which applies well beyond the case of the גֵּר.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: where he is not in his courtyard,
he does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 16 into the final practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A courtyard does not acquire for an owner who is not present.

steps.title: New משנה: a pit dug in one domain and opened into another
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who digs a בּוֹר in one domain and opens it into a different domain is liable for damage it causes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who digs a pit on private property and opens it into the public domain, or digs in the public domain and opens it onto private property, or digs on private property and opens it onto someone else's private property, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three cases where the pit is dug in one place but its opening is in another place, and in all of them the digger is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three cases are: from רשות היחיד into רשות הרבים, from רשות הרבים into רשות היחיד, and from his own רשות היחיד into someone else's. In each one the pit crosses from one domain into another, and the משנה says the digger pays for the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
One who digs a pit
Private property
Public domain
Its opening
Liable to pay

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who digs a pit on private property
and opens it into the public domain,
or digs in the public domain
and opens it onto private property,
or digs on private property
and opens it onto another person's private property, is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the collateral discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Digging a pit in one domain with its opening in another domain makes the digger liable.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: this is the pit the Torah talks about
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the cases of the משנה and says, in the name of רבי ישמעאל, that this is the בּוֹר the Torah talks about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: One who digs a pit on private property and opens it into the public domain, or in the public domain and opens it onto private property, is liable, and this is the pit stated in the Torah. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches the משנה. It adds that, according to רבי ישמעאל, these cases are the בּוֹר the Torah is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said the digger is liable. The ברייתא adds who said it and goes further: רבי ישמעאל says this kind of pit is the very case of בּוֹר in the Torah. This sets up the disagreement with רבי עקיבא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The pit stated in the Torah

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
One who digs a pit on private property
and opens it into the public domain;
or in the public domain and opens it onto private property,
is liable, and this is the pit stated in the Torah;
phrases.notes: This means the pit in שמות 21:33.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that matches the משנה and names רבי ישמעאל as its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: a pit that crosses between private and public property is the בּוֹר the Torah talks about.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the Torah's pit is one on ownerless land
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the בּוֹר of the Torah is the case of someone who gave up ownership of his land but not of his pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: If he gave up ownership of his property but did not give up ownership of his pit, that is the pit stated in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל about which case the Torah's בּוֹר refers to. For him it is a person who made his land הפקר but kept his pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל points to a pit that crosses between private and public property. רבי עקיבא points to a different case: the land around the pit becomes ownerless, while the pit still belongs to him. Each one names a different case as the main case of בּוֹר in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave up ownership (made ownerless)
His property
His pit

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: the Torah's בּוֹר is a pit that crosses between private and public property. רבי עקיבא: it is a pit whose owner gave up his land but kept the pit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
If he gave up ownership of his property but did not give up ownership of his pit,
this is the pit stated in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הִפְקִיר רְשׁוּתוֹ וְלֹא הִפְקִיר בּוֹרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, disagreeing view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: the Torah's בּוֹר is a pit kept by its owner after he made his land ownerless.

steps.title: רבה: Everyone agrees a pit in the public domain makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that for a בּוֹר in רשות הרבים, both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree the digger is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: If the pit is in the public domain, everyone agrees that the person is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins explaining the argument from the ברייתא. First he names the case where both sides agree: a pit dug in the public domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argued about which pit is "the בּוֹר of the Torah." רבה narrows the argument by saying it does not touch a pit in רשות הרבים. There, all agree the digger pays.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, an area everyone uses, like a street
Everyone, meaning both opinions in the argument
They do not disagree
He is liable, meaning he must pay

phrases.english: Rabba said:
With a pit in the public domain –
everyone agrees that he is liable,
phrases.notes: "Everyone" here means both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא from the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בְּבוֹר בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the argument between רבי ישמעאל (Step 19) and רבי עקיבא (Step 20) by first naming where they agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pit in the public domain makes the digger liable according to all opinions.

steps.title: Why is he liable in the public domain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of liability for a pit in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why everyone agrees he is liable for a pit in public ground. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person does not own the street, so we might think he is not responsible for a pit there. The question asks what makes him liable anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבה's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that one is liable for a pit in public ground he does not own.

steps.title: The verse's double wording: opening and digging
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says both "כי יפתח" and "כי יכרה". Since digging is obviously worse than opening, the extra word teaches that liability comes from the act itself, not from owning the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "If a man shall open" and "if a man shall dig." If he is liable for opening, is he not all the more so liable for digging?! Rather, the pit becomes his responsibility through the act of opening and the act of digging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the פסוק. It points out that the word "dig" seems extra, and explains what that extra word teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening a pit someone else already dug is a smaller act than digging a new one. So mentioning digging seems unneeded, since it would follow by a קל וחומר. The answer is that the Torah is teaching where liability comes from: the act of opening or digging makes the pit his responsibility, even in רשות הרבים where he owns nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Opening, meaning uncovering an existing pit
Digging a new pit
All the more so, a קל וחומר
Through the matter of, by way of doing

steps.confusionAlert: The question "is it not all the more so?!" is not an attack on רבה. It is part of reading the פסוק: it shows the extra word, so we know the פסוק is teaching something new.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for saying a person can be liable for a hazard on land he does not own. His own act of making the pit is what makes him responsible.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"If a man shall open" and "if a man shall dig" –
if he is liable for opening,
is he not all the more so liable for digging?!
Rather, through the act of opening
and through the act of digging, it came to him.
phrases.notes: "It came to him" means the pit became his responsibility, even though the ground is not his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: כִּי יִפְתַּח וְכִי יִכְרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22 with a reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word "dig" teaches that liability comes from the act of opening or digging, not from owning the land. So one is liable even in the public domain.

steps.title: רבה begins to say where they do disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבה starts to name the case where רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא really argue. The sentence continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree only…
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the agreed case is settled, רבה starts to say where the real argument is. This line sets up the next move, which continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the public-domain pit is agreed upon, the argument must be about a different case. רבה is about to name it, likely one involving a person's own property.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagreed only about…

phrases.english: They disagree only

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the agreed case, רבה moves to point out the real area of argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא is limited to a specific case other than the public-domain pit; the case is named in the next lines.
